## Shared context (verbatim, immutable)

# Review context: scope-termination determinism and JoinPolicy.AWAIT_ALL

Range: 729cb874 (dev/v0.5.0 tip) .. HEAD of branch feat/join-policy-await-all, five commits:

1. `fix: derive the scope termination from frozen results, not settle order` (stage A). Removes the
   arrival-order `ScopeTerminationAccumulator`. `TaskBatch#deriveScopeTermination` and
   `TaskGroup#deriveScopeTermination`/`failedTask` derive the scope termination at freeze /
   convergence: first FAILED in input/declaration order outranks every cancellation; then the
   group's direct-member and caller rules, then the token's committed state.
2. `test: keep the convergence test name and except the removed accumulator test`.
3. `feat: add a per-scope join policy with AWAIT_ALL` (stage B). Public `JoinPolicy` enum,
   `BatchOptions.joinPolicy`, `GroupStart.joinPolicy`. `CancellationToken.bind` picks
   `allAsList` (FAIL_FAST) or `successfulAsList` (AWAIT_ALL); token state `SUCCESS` renamed
   `COMPLETED`. `TaskGroup.memberCompleted` skips the direct-cancel cascade under AWAIT_ALL and
   `skipCombineAfterAllMembersSettled` cancels a declared combine via `groupToken.failFastCancel()`
   once every member settled with a non-success. `Par.executeCombined` does the same for
   `mapAndCombine` via a `successfulAsList(views)` listener.
4. `test: match the fail-fast commit-order mutation to the policy-guarded callback`.
5. `refactor: tighten the join-policy derivations and their test setup` (refactoring-review
   items R2-R5; R1 deferred). Treat these as settled; check behavior preservation of commit 5.

Owning contracts (read the changed sections): `design/task-termination-and-scope.md` section 4,
`design/cancellation-propagation.md` sections 1 and 1.1, `design/task-group-cancellation.md` 8.2-8.3,
`design/batch-terminal-combine.md`, `design/task-group-terminal-combine.md` section 8. User docs:
`docs/en/user-guide.md` (#join-policy, #scope-termination), `docs/en/design/idea-graveyard.md`.

Do not read `verification/contract-tests/`.

Attack surfaces:

- Interleavings: member settle vs group convergence barrier (`completedTasks`), the nested
  combine completion inside `failFastCancel`, `settledMembers`/`memberSuccesses` publication,
  deadline/cancelOn/parent cancellation racing the last member settle under AWAIT_ALL,
  `successfulAsList(views)` listener vs the batch token's own aggregate, sliding-window refill
  after a failure, direct-executor and inline execution paths.
- Contract versus implementation: diff every MUST/MUST NOT in the commit messages and in
  `cancellation-propagation.md` section 1.1 and `task-termination-and-scope.md` section 4 against
  the code line by line, including attribution reasons and their source identities.
- Behavior changes for existing FAIL_FAST callers: anything that changed when the policy is the
  default (scope termination precedence, failedTaskName, values future, report strings).
- Test quality: do the new tests (`AwaitAllJoinPolicyTest`, `ScopeTerminationOrderTest`) fail
  without the code they guard; are any of them timing-dependent or vacuous.
- Java 8 API use in `core/src/main/java`, generics, nullability (JSpecify/NullAway).

summary: Reviewed all five commits across token binding, scope termination, terminal combines, contracts, and tests. The main defect is that FAIL_FAST direct member cancellation still takes the legacy CANCELLED path; additional issues affect AWAIT_ALL logging, shutdown and contract documentation, and timing-dependent tests.

findings.title: FAIL_FAST direct member cancellation does not commit FAIL_FAST
findings.trigger: Submit a default-FAIL_FAST group with two pending adopted futures and cancel the first member directly.
findings.consequence: The sibling is cancelled, but its frozen reason is CANCELLED_BY_PARENT_SCOPE and the group token is CANCELLED, rather than the documented FAIL_FAST and ABORTED_BY_FAIL_FAST attribution.
findings.evidence: TaskGroup.memberCompleted calls cancelGroupAndUnfinishedMembers at TaskGroup.java:870; that method uses groupToken.cancel() at TaskGroup.java:913. TokenOutcomes.java:53 maps CANCELLED to CANCELLED_BY_PARENT_SCOPE. This contradicts JoinPolicy.java:16 and design/cancellation-propagation.md:74; TaskGroupTest.java:517 currently pins the legacy result.
findings.suggestedFix: Use groupToken.failFastCancel() for this path and update the direct-cancellation regression to assert ABORTED_BY_FAIL_FAST while retaining CANCELLED_BY_MEMBER for the scope. If legacy attribution is intended instead, narrow the new Javadocs and contracts consistently.

findings.title: AWAIT_ALL retains allAsList paths that log ordinary failures at SEVERE
findings.trigger: Run mapAndCombine with AWAIT_ALL and at least two failing elements, or call valuesOrThrow() on an AWAIT_ALL map containing two failures.
findings.consequence: Guava logs each failure after the first at SEVERE with 'Got more than one input Future failure', turning expected per-element outcomes into alert noise and unnecessary stack-trace generation.
findings.evidence: Par.java:253 uses Futures.allAsList(views) as the AWAIT_ALL combine gate. TaskBatchResult.java:324 similarly builds Futures.allAsList(results) before manually selecting the first failure. AwaitAllJoinPolicyTest.java:65 explicitly disables AggregateFuture logging instead of preventing it.
findings.suggestedFix: Under AWAIT_ALL, gate the combine through one non-logging all-settle aggregate with explicit outcome inspection. Implement valuesOrThrow() as orThrow() followed by direct value collection rather than constructing allAsList(results).

findings.title: Public close() guidance conflicts with ParRuntime.close semantics
findings.trigger: A caller follows the new guide and invokes ParRuntime.close() while a batch or group still has unfinished members.
findings.consequence: Admitted members keep running: ParRuntime.close() rejects new work and drains services rather than cancelling scopes, contrary to the new promise that close() cancels every unfinished member.
findings.evidence: docs/en/user-guide.md:129 and docs/en/user-guide.md:206 make the unqualified cancellation promise, also present at JoinPolicy.java:8. ParRuntime.java:383 only marks the runtime closed and schedules service shutdown; cancellation exists only on package-private TaskBatch.close() and TaskGroup.close() at TaskBatch.java:415 and TaskGroup.java:438.
findings.suggestedFix: Disambiguate internal scope close from runtime shutdown in the public guide and JoinPolicy Javadoc. If ParRuntime.close() is intended to cancel admitted work, change that behavior only through an explicit runtime-contract decision.

findings.title: Cancellation contract still specifies the removed cancellation-first derivation
findings.trigger: A group deadline, caller cancellation, or parent cancellation commits before a member failure is recorded before convergence.
findings.consequence: This chapter still predicts a cancellation-shaped scope and says later business failures do not overwrite it, while the implementation now reports FAILED with that failure.
findings.evidence: design/task-group-cancellation.md:18 and design/task-group-cancellation.md:157 retain the old single-CAS/token-first rules. TaskGroup.java:1056 checks the first recorded FAILED task before any token state, matching the new priority in design/task-termination-and-scope.md:203.
findings.suggestedFix: Rewrite the chapter to the frozen failure-first derivation: remove the single-CAS and late-failure-no-overwrite wording and state that the first failure in declaration order outranks every committed cancellation.

findings.title: Lifecycle and adoption contracts omit AWAIT_ALL exceptions
findings.trigger: An AWAIT_ALL group member fails or is directly cancelled while siblings remain pending.
findings.consequence: The lifecycle rules still say every non-success cancels siblings and every direct cancellation cascades, but the implementation lets siblings finish; callers following these contracts incorrectly expect group-wide cancellation.
findings.evidence: design/task-group-lifecycle.md:247 and design/task-group-lifecycle.md:249 are unqualified. TaskGroup.java:870 guards the cascade with FAIL_FAST, while TaskGroup.java:893 only skips the terminal combine under AWAIT_ALL. GroupStart.java:65 likewise says a failure cancels adopted sources without the policy qualification.
findings.suggestedFix: Qualify both lifecycle rules and the adopted-source documentation with FAIL_FAST, then explicitly state that AWAIT_ALL member failure or direct cancellation leaves siblings and their sources running.

findings.title: New deadline and ordering tests depend on uncontrolled wall-clock timing
findings.trigger: A loaded CI runner pauses worker startup or group submission for more than 200 milliseconds, or the caller does not reach WAITING within ten seconds in ScopeTerminationOrderTest.
findings.consequence: The deadline tests can record DEADLINE_EXCEEDED before the required failure or success, producing false CI failures; the end-to-end ordering helper can silently skip its intended interleaving and weaken its reproduction.
findings.evidence: The group test starts a 200 ms deadline at AwaitAllJoinPolicyTest.java:292 before asserting an already-recorded failure at line 299. The batch test does the same at line 448 before asserting its failure at line 451. ScopeTerminationOrderTest.java:112 returns without any assertion when its ten-second wait expires.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a controllable Ticker or manual deadline scheduler and advance time only after the required outcomes are recorded. Make awaitCallerParked fail on timeout or replace it with a deterministic handshake that guarantees the batch object exists before the later element settles.
